_comment: Single source of truth for consensus-affecting constants whose drift between C++ and Rust would cause silent wrong-output (rather than fail-closed-on-load). Generated into both languages by cmake/generate_consensus_constants.py (C++) and rust/shekyl-engine-core/build.rs / rust/shekyl-difficulty/build.rs (Rust). Hand-maintained values on either side have been deleted and replaced with `static_assert` sentinels against the generated values. Bug class motivated by Bug 3 of the 2026-05-05 FFI constant-drift audit (see docs/audit_trail/2026-05-ffi-constant-drift-audit.md). Adding entries: keep the audit doc's 'Constants confirmed aligned' table in sync with this file. MEMBERSHIP RULE (docs/design/CLIENT_VERSION_CONSTANTS_VALIDATION.md §3.7, VC-D7): only a constant whose different value makes a DIFFERENT CHAIN belongs here. The canonical form of this file (every non-underscore key, bytewise-sorted, one `key value` line each) is digested into CONSENSUS_CONSTANTS_DIGEST by rust/shekyl-rpc-types/build.rs; once slices VC-2..VC-4 of that design land, every client will compare it against the daemon at connect, so a tunable placed here would make every client refuse every daemon built after it moved. Keys beginning with an underscore are prose and are excluded from the digest; every other value must be a non-negative integer, or the build fails.
_comment_daa: LWMA-1 difficulty adjustment parameters per docs/completed/DAA_LWMA1.md §4. Consumed by rust/shekyl-difficulty (Phase 1, ratified 2026-05-18). Window-shape constants only: N, T, FTL, MTP window length, and the genesis difficulty constant. The bias factor 99/200, the solvetime clamp 6, and the min-L floor 1/20 deliberately do NOT live here per the Round 3 disposition (DAA_LWMA1.md §4) — they appear as bare integer literals inside src/lwma1.rs because changing them is a deviation from the canonical zawy12 reference, not a tunable parameter. daa_genesis_difficulty is the launch-calibration knob for the first N blocks (LWMA-1 short-circuit until the window is full); retune it here. 400 is the 2026-09-11 testnet calibration against skl-miner-test (4 RandomX v2 threads): D=100 produced ~20s blocks, so 400 is ~80–120s on that miner. The zawy12 example value of 100 remains the historical Round-4 pin in DAA_LWMA1.md §2.6.
_comment_block_weight: Short-term block-weight surge factor S: the effective median may exceed the long-term effective median by at most S (100-block fast governor). Ratified S = 4 (CONSENSUS_C2_R2_WEIGHT_FEES.md Q3, signed 2026-09-06). Loosening S reopens Q2: during the first ~100000 blocks this bound is the only protection against early-chain weight growth. Owner: shekyl-economics::effective_median / shekyl_effective_block_weight_median.
_comment_archival: Per-shard archival retention bond floor (ARCHIVAL_BOND_FLOOR). Calibrated from bond_rate* = 0.75 per docs/design/FOUNDATION_GENESIS_IDENTITY_SET.md §9.3 (1 sim capital unit ≡ 1 SKL). Foundation CompleteTree holders post one nominal bond at this floor.
_comment_archival_timing: Archival timing cluster per docs/design/ARCHIVAL_TIMING_CONSTANTS.md §6 (pinned 2026-06-07). max_claim_age_w wired into KEYS_INTEGER / generate_consensus_constants.py (ArchivalBondValue v4 decode invariants) and rust/shekyl-archival-retention/build.rs; remaining keys wire at their consumers during PHASE_2B implementation. archival_reorg_depth_blocks is additionally consumed as SP-R0 arm #1's prune-permanence canonicity floor (ARCHIVAL_BOND_SP_R0_PLAN.md §4, rule-21 registration 2026-07-18): the P-scan ingest ceiling trails tip by this depth, so prune-at-ingest of spent funding records is reorg-safe ONLY at this depth or deeper — LOWERING this value reopens arm #1's prune-at-ingest safety (a smaller ceiling prunes wallet funding records before they are reorg-safe); do not retune it for faster finality without re-running that round. Third consumer (ARCHIVAL_SHARD_FETCH.md SF-D8, 2026-09-13): it is the pass-countersignature ANCHOR DEPTH — a requester anchors its shard read to block_hash(tip − this) and admission accepts anchor heights in [h − this − archival_attestation_anchor_lag_blocks, h − this] for a block whose predecessor is h. Both directions are dangerous here, not one: LOWERING it makes the signed anchor hash reorg-sensitive (a burial shallower than the freeze margin can be replaced, so honest passes miss on a fork — the same 'frozen at this depth' assumption segment freeze already makes); RAISING it lengthens collusive pre-signing lead one block per block (a colluding P can sign hash(T) the moment T exists and hold a signature usable at T + depth). PDM-Q11's D_max reorg gate has this as a consumer: a reorg deeper than this depth moves a canonical anchor hash and invalidates admitted passes.
_comment_archival_attestation_anchor_lag: PROVISIONAL L = 4 (ARCHIVAL_SHARD_FETCH.md SF-D8, ruled 2026-09-13). Admission accepts a pass whose anchor_height lies in [h − archival_reorg_depth_blocks − L, h − archival_reorg_depth_blocks], h the predecessor of the block carrying the record; P's pre-sign gate (RF-R1, lands with SF §9.1 step (a)) accepts anchor_height within ±L of its own (height − depth), the SAME L both sides so no P gates distinctively. L covers fetch span plus P/requester skew: two blocks of fetch-plus-SF-D6-retry (~4 min), one block of skew, one block of margin. The asymmetry decides the direction: too SMALL produces honest witness misses (unpriced, landing on operators); too LARGE costs one block of pre-fetch lead per unit against a 720-block floor and one block of epoch slack per unit against 10000. FALSIFIER: the W2 / PD-F-2 fetch-latency dispersion measurement. If p99 fetch-plus-retry lands under two minutes, drop to 3. If it lands over six minutes the answer is NOT to raise L — L would then be absorbing what SF-D6's retry budget should bound; tighten the budget instead. Minimum 2 (a fetch spanning one block boundary must not miss), enforced by rust/shekyl-archival-retention/build.rs. Consumed by shekyl-archival-retention::attestation_wire (Rust-only authority); C++ sizes the anchor-hash window through shekyl_archival_pass_anchor_window rather than a generated header constant, so there is ONE authority and no drift pair.
_comment_archival_failure_window: Sliding-window m-of-n archival failure confirmation (docs/completed/ARCHIVAL_FAILURE_CONFIRMATION_PIN.md §1). Shape genesis-frozen (slash iff m misses fall within the last n baseline OBSERVATIONS for a (P_id, shard); no per-P confirmation FSM, no post-miss recheck — a predictable recheck is the dodge surface §5 rejects); numerics PROVISIONAL at the Round-1 values, re-pinned at the Round-2 testnet stressnet against the measured outage-duration CDF (pin §3.2 four-criterion joint gate). The bond_duration precedent: shape frozen, numerics re-pinnable. Consumer is Rust-only (shekyl-archival-retention::failure_window); C++ reads m/n through shekyl_archival_failure_window_params rather than a generated header constant, so there is ONE authority and no drift pair to keep aligned.
_comment_bond_duration: Per-shard retention-commitment horizon (gate-4 §4.4; ARCHIVAL_TIMING_CONSTANTS.md §1). Shape genesis-frozen (age-scaled-constant: bond_duration(age) = BASE * (1 + SCALE * age)); numerics provisional (H2 plateau arm, re-pin at testnet within scale band [2,8]). Age is shard_age_milli evaluated at the shard's add-epoch settlement close H_close(add_epoch) = (add_epoch+1)*SEB (NOT a raw within-epoch add block height; the age-realization invariant), computed once at acquisition.
_comment_archival_reward_path: D3/R2: production credited work is linear in work (credited_work_milli). The retired banded-PL plateau lives only as a sim/counterfactual in reward_arithmetic::curve_milli — not a consensus config key.
_comment_archival_reward_age_weight: g(age) slope on relative-depth age (ARCHIVAL_REWARD_ARITHMETIC.md §Shard age). Sealed target g* ≈ 2; calibration band [1500, 2500] per the Layer-2 margin-robustness run (STAKER_ARCHIVAL_SIM.md).
_comment_archival_segment: Segment/shard geometry (ARCHIVAL_SEGMENT_FREEZE_PIPELINE.md §5.2). SEGMENT_LEAF_COUNT is the level-2 subtree leaf count under the production curve-tree widths — 38 * 18 * 38 = 25992 (CURVE_TREE_CLIENT.md §7.2.2; gate-2 §2 'Genesis provisional: subtree level 2'). NOT a tunable: rust/shekyl-archival-retention/src/segment_freeze.rs carries a compile-time assert tying this value to shekyl_fcmp::tree::leaves_per_segment() — the one partition derivation both the wallet-side shard store and the consensus reader take from that crate (V3_WALLET_DECISION_LOG.md 2026-09-17, two stores) — so neither a width change nor an edit here can silently move pop revert away from the store (corrected 2026-09-19: NOT bond admission, which reads frozen_segment_count nowhere — its shard predicate was ruled 2026-09-19 and is unbuilt, docs/design/ARCHIVAL_BOND_ADD_ADMISSION.md). 'Genesis provisional' above is the gate-2 era label; the freeze pipeline round pinned level 2. Consumed by the freeze first-crossing rule (frozen = leaf_count / segment_leaf_count) and the challenge-path leaf-chunk derivation; the boundary division lives ONLY in the Rust entry point (both C++ hooks call the FFI — division one-site tripwire).
